entries.title: The direct act and the cause: on whom the ḍamān of an itlāf falls

statement.note: Ibn Rajab, qāʿida 127: an itlāf resting on a direct act and a cause makes the direct act liable, «إلا إذا كانت المباشرة مبنية على السبب وناشئة عنه»; then the cause alone bears it where the direct act has no transgression, and shares it where it has some. «فالأقسام ثلاثة».

refs.note: Division one: pushing someone into a well another dug in transgression, «فالضمان على الدافع وحده».
Division two: the judge's execution arises from false testimony without transgression in him, «فالضمان والقود عليهم دون الحاكم».
Division three, on one riwāya: «الممسك مع القاتل فإنهما يشتركان في الضمان والقود على إحدى الروايتين»; the other riwāya gives it to the direct actor alone.

conditions: an itlāf of persons or property resting on both a direct act (mubāshara) and a cause (sabab)
whether the direct act is built on the cause and arises from it
whether the direct act has any transgression
entries.rationale: The IslamQA tranche left 9 of its 27 itlāf cases as missing_rule with need rule:mubashara_tasabbub: these answers turn on causation, which the itlāf encoder (al-Saʿdī Q13 ⊔ Q36) does not read. Ibn Rajab's qāʿida 127 states that rule over itlāf itself, with three divisions its own furūʿ instance. It is formalised as a new encoder beside itlāf, which is unchanged; its type extends itlāf's types (Usul.Typing.Qaida.Mubashara). A cause with no direct act is not covered by the statement and stays a gap.
